_session: Exegete Passage 1, Day One (2026-08-18), question CC-EX1

captures.text: Okay, Martin's exegesis notes for Passage 1. He's got the shape of the passage down, he marked the two places where the repetition falls and he wrote a line about why it's there, which is more than I expected on day one. Where it thins out is the difficult terms. There are two words in this passage that don't have an obvious equivalent and he hasn't touched either of them. When I asked him what he'd tell a drafter about verse six he had to go back and reread before he could answer. So a drafter could work from these notes for most of it and would be guessing in two places.

Jael's notes. Honestly these are the ones I'd hand to a drafter tomorrow without a conversation. She's written the passage out in her own words first and then gone back and flagged the places where her wording drifts from the source, and said why it drifts. She caught the shift in who's speaking in the middle section, which nobody else in the room caught, and she wrote a note to the drafter about it rather than just marking it for herself. She also wrote down two questions she couldn't answer, which is the thing I keep telling people to do and almost nobody does on the first day.

Sibaji. His notes are mostly a restatement of the passage. He's gone verse by verse and written what each verse says, which is fine as far as it goes, but there's nothing in there about why anything is there or what a drafter would actually need to decide. No flags, no questions, nothing on the difficult terms. When I sat with him he clearly knows more than the notes show, he told me about the tension between the two speakers straight away, but none of that made it onto the page. I'd have to sit with him for twenty minutes before I could draft from this.

Micah's Passage 1 notes. He's done the background work, there's a paragraph on the historical setting that's genuinely useful, but the notes about the passage itself are thin and in a couple of places I think he's wrong. He's read verse four as a command when the form is closer to an invitation, and that changes what a drafter would do with it. He also hasn't distinguished between what he's confident about and what he's guessing at, so a drafter reading this would take the guesses for settled. I'd want to go back through this section with him before anyone drafts from it.

Coming back to Martin at the end of the session. He went back to the two difficult terms after we talked and wrote up both of them. He's given a literal gloss, what he thinks it means here, and one alternative a drafter could use if the first one doesn't work in the language. That's the thing that was missing this morning. And he didn't ask me what to write, he asked Jael, which I want to note because it's the first time anyone in the room has used their partner that way.
